title: Marketplace funds can be drained due to lack of auction payout accounting
reason: Missing auction payout accounting lets a caller drain marketplace funds.

title: mintWithSignature() front-running vulnerability
reason: A front-runner can consume a signed mint and receive the token instead of the intended recipient.

title: Any signer can withdraw the smart wallet’s deposit amount
reason: Any active signer can move the smart wallet's deposit, so one signer can take the account's funds.

title: Unsafe listing update allows seller front-run to buyer purchase
reason: The seller can update the listing to front-run a purchase and extract extra payment from the buyer.

title: OFT Decimals Should Match decimalPlaces
reason: Hardcoded 18 OFT decimals inflates amounts bridged from 6-decimal chains, minting unbacked value on the destination.

title: Rollover Bids Bypass Initial Collateral Ratio Enabling Self Liquidation
reason: Rollover bids skip the initial collateral check; the borrower keeps inflated proceeds while lenders absorb the shortfall.

title: Arbitrary Function Execution In retrieveFunds Enables Complete Protocol Compromise
reason: Attacker-supplied retrieveFunds calldata is executed with functionCall on the diamond, reaching privileged facet functions and user funds.

title: Missing Access Control In TermMorphoInterfaceFacet Allows Unauthorised Position Manipulation
reason: All facet functions except the signature setter lack caller validation; an attacker manipulates victim Morpho positions and collects liquidation bonuses.

title: Bid Update Collateral Array Mutation Enables Cross-User Locker Drain
reason: _lock() diffs collateral by array index without token identity, so a mutated update unlocks another token and drains the shared locker.

title: Uninitialised AccessControl In TermDiamond
reason: Missing AccessControl init breaks role checks and causes functionality failures (DoS); no attacker value path is described.

title: Wrong-Token retrieveFunds() Drains Diamond Balances Via Ignored Asset Check
reason: Settlement treats any retrieveFunds callback as proof of arrival; a wrong-token callback makes it spend the diamond's existing balances.

title: Partial Liquidation Net Exposure Cap Guard Always Bypassed, Enabling Bad Debt Creation
reason: The net-exposure guard early-returns true; two batchLiquidation calls seize all collateral at a discount and leave lenders with bad debt.

title: BuniCornPool.swap lacks access and balance checks; callback only when calldata > 0
reason: Swap has no access or balance check and skips the callback for empty calldata, so an attacker can swap without paying and drain the pool.

title: BuniCornPool.mint callable by anyone enables minting to arbitrary address
reason: Anyone can call mint with a victim and an attacker-chosen recipient, minting the victim's coins to the attacker.

title: BuniCornPool.burn callable by anyone enables taking others’ coins
reason: Duplicate: burn is permissionless and, with favourable timing, pays the caller another user's coins.

title: BuniCornPool.burn is publicly callable and can transfer others’ coins
reason: Anyone can call burn and be paid out based on pool state, receiving tokens belonging to another user.

title: BuniCornRouter02.removeLiquidity should be private; does not account received liquidity
reason: Public removeLiquidity does not account the LP received, so the caller can take the surplus balance.

title: BuniCornRouter02.removeLiquidity should be private; ignores actual LP received leading to potential loss
reason: Duplicate: public removeLiquidity ignores actual LP received and leaves surplus for the caller.

title: BuniCornPool.mint is publicly callable and can mint to arbitrary addresses
reason: Duplicate: public mint to an arbitrary recipient lets the caller take another user's coins.

title: previousPrices Is Never Updated Upon Syncing Token Price
reason: Stale LiquidityBasedTWAP prices may misprice liquidity, but the excerpt does not quantify an attacker edge.

title: VaderPoolV2 minting synths & fungibles can be frontrun
reason: Front-running a victim mint with from=victim and to=attacker pulls the victim's deposit and delivers the synths to the attacker.

title: Using single total native reserve variable for synth and non-synth reserves of VaderPoolV2 can lead to losses for synth holders
reason: An LP withdraws a pro-rata slice that includes synth backing, leaving synth minters unable to redeem.

title: Redemption value of synths can be manipulated to drain VaderPoolV2 of all native assets in the associated pair
reason: Flash-swap to inflate the native price, mint synths, reverse the swap and burn at the cheap price; the pair's native reserves are drained.

title: totalLiquidityWeight Is Updated When Adding New Token Pairs Which Skews Price Data For getVaderPrice and getUSDVPrice
reason: Adding a pair inflates totalLiquidityWeight before past weights adjust; an attacker trades against the skewed VADER/USDV price.

title: Reserve does not properly apply prices of VADER and USDV tokens
reason: Wrong fixed-point scaling in VaderReserve over- or under-pays; the excess can be taken.

title: USDV.sol Mint and Burn Amounts Are Incorrect
reason: Mint/burn mixes USD-denominated prices, letting the caller mint or burn at the wrong ratio.

title: H-10. Stealing any loan opening for auction through others' lending pool
reason: buyLoan with someone else's poolId makes that pool pay the debt while the attacker becomes the new lender.

title: H-07. Borrower can bypass maxLoanRatio's configuration of a pool via buyLoan()
reason: Borrow at high LTV then force the loan into a pool with a lower maxLoanRatio, over-borrowing against the collateral.

title: H-02. Lender contract can be drained by re-entrancy in `repay`
reason: Collateral is transferred before the loan is deleted, so a token hook reenters repay and receives collateral repeatedly.

title: H-08. Lender#buyLoan - Malicious user could take over a loan for free without having a pool because of wrong access control
reason: buyLoan sets loans[loanId].lender=msg.sender without pool ownership, so the caller takes over the loan for free.

title: H-03. Lender contract can be drained by re-entrancy in `setPool`
reason: Reentering setPool through a callback token before the storage update repeats the payout.

title: H-04. Sandwich attack to steal all ERC-20 tokens in the Fees contract
reason: Fees.sellProfits swaps with amountOutMinimum=0, so a sandwich buys the profit tokens at an arbitrarily bad price and captures the balance.

title: H-09. Using forged/fake lending pools to steal any loan opening for auction
reason: buyLoan does not verify the new pool's loanToken/collateralToken against the loan, so a forged pool steals the loan.

title: Issue H-5: Curve V2 Vaults can be drained because CurveV2CryptoEthOracle can be reentered with WETH tokens
reason: The read-only reentrancy guard covers the ETH sentinel but Curve V2 pools use WETH; reentering the oracle at a manipulated price drains the vault.

title: Issue H-10: Immediately start getting rewards belonging to others after staking
reason: Staking just before a reward accrual captures rewards earned by prior stakers.

title: Issue H-11: Differences between actual and cached total assets can be arbitraged
reason: Deposit while cached assets understate the vault, then trigger a debt update so totalAssets rises and redeem at the higher share price.

title: Issue H-6: updateDebtReporting can be front run, putting all the loss on later withdrawals but taking the profit
reason: The caller chooses which destination vaults to report, realizes only gains, withdraws, and leaves losses to later LPs.

title: Issue H-15: Maverick oracle can be manipulated
reason: A flash loan shifts Maverick reserves and moves the MavEthOracle price used to value LP positions.

title: Issue H-12: Gain From LMPVault Can Be Stolen
reason: The report describes theft of LMPVault gains; the exact call sequence is not fixed by the available excerpt.

title: Issue H-1: ETH deposited by the user may be stolen.
reason: When paying with ETH the router wraps msg.value and pullToken also pulls WETH, leaving excess WETH that can be swept with sweepToken.

title: BBLiquidation/SGLLiquidation::_updateBorrowAndCollateralShare liquidator can bypass bad debt handling to ensure whole liquidation reward
reason: A small maxBorrowPart keeps collateral covering the repay slice, so the liquidator takes the full reward while bad debt stays with the protocol.

title: Recursive _lzCompose() call can be leveraged to steal all generated USDO fees
reason: A nested compose from the USDO contract bypasses allowance and re-mints the USDO fees to the attacker on the destination chain.

title: Unverified _srcChainSender parameter allows to impersonate the sender
reason: _srcChainSender is not verified for several message types, so a compose message can act as any source-chain sender.

title: Unprotected executeModule function allows to steal the tokens
reason: Anyone can call Usdo.executeModule with an arbitrary module/data and invoke whitelisted Magnetar paths as the victim.

title: Malicious MarketHelper contract can be used in TOFTMarketReceiverModule's leverageUpReceiver and marketRemoveCollateralReceiver functions
reason: The MarketHelper is not validated, so an attacker-controlled helper executes arbitrary market actions against user positions.

title: Pending allowances can be exploited
reason: Front-running a user's pending allowance lets the attacker borrow or withdraw on their behalf.

title: exerciseOptionsReceiver() Lack of Ownership Check for oTAP, Allowing Anyone to Use oTAPTokenID
reason: Only the permit is checked, not oTAP ownership, so an attacker can front-run and exercise another user's option.

title: updateAllPositionFromBalanceMargin function mistakenly increments positions "fromBalance"
reason: updateAllPositionFromBalanceMargin adds the full change to every position, inflating fromBalance so the trader can withdraw more than entitled.

title: Excess fromBalance removal not added to other positions fromBalance's when leveraging up
reason: Removed excess fromBalance is not redistributed, inflating remaining available value that the trader can withdraw.

title: Pool value calculation skips accounting for stable token losses and short uPnL
reason: Pool value omits stable-token losses and short uPnL, overstating share value so redeemers extract more than their share.

title: Attacker can inflate stake rewards as he wants.
reason: FeeRewardsProcess.updateAccountFeeRewards reads the live balanceOf, so a flash/transfer-inflated balance inflates the account's fee rewards paid from the pool.

title: Incorrect implementation of the PositionMarginProcess.updatePositionFromBalanceMargin() function.
reason: Early return in updatePositionFromBalanceMargin blocks the fromBalance reduction, leaving margin overstated and withdrawable.

title: Pool value does not consider the open funding fees
reason: Pool value ignores unsettled funding fees, so shares are minted/redeemed at a stale value and the difference is captured by the depositor/redeemer.

title: Cross available value is not accounting the position fees
reason: Accrued position fees are not deducted from cross available value, letting the trader withdraw/borrow against overstated equity and leave bad debt.

title: H-15. ReseedBarn.sol doesn't initialize of `s.sys.fert.recapitalized`
reason: Missing fert.recapitalized initialization misprices Unripe conversions, but the released text does not establish a concrete attacker payout without post-migration state.

title: H-05. Successful transactions are not stored, causing a replay attack on redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances
reason: Merkle leaf is never marked redeemed and signatures carry no per-user nonce, so the same proof/signature can be replayed to re-credit stalk/roots repeatedly.

title: H-03. LibUsdOracle returns the wrong price for Uniswap Oracle
reason: Base/quote roles are swapped and decimals assumed 6, quoting USDC in WBTC or mis-scaling an 18-decimal quote so positions are mispriced.

title: H-02. LibUsdOracle will compromise Beanstalk peg due to wrong price and DoS
reason: Chainlink result is inverted and scaled twice, returning inflated prices (and reverting on a zero answer), so conversions are mispriced in the caller's favour.

title: H-01. LibChainlinkOracle::getTokenPrice will always return instantaneous prices
reason: The ternary is inverted so the oracle always returns the instantaneous price, allowing flash manipulation before deposit/borrow/liquidation.

title: H-19. `ReseedSilo` does not set the necessary user variables
reason: Reseed leaves lastUpdated/lastSop/lastRain unset, so mowing over-accrues Plenty that the caller can claim.

title: H-22. Incorrect calculation of `beanUsdPrice` in LibEvaluate::evalPrice
reason: beanUsdPrice is dimensionally wrong, so mint/redeem decisions are taken at the wrong price and the difference is extractable.

title: H-13. Missing abort status check allows bid taker to steal users funds
reason: Missing abort-status check lets a bid taker settle an aborted offer and take the user's funds.

title: H-12. Fund Withdrawal Flaw in preMarket Allows Users to Avoid Settlement Obligations
reason: Seller withdraws credited SalesRevenue/TaxIncome and then declines to deliver at settlement, keeping the buyer's funds.

title: H-07. Malicious user can drain protocol by bypassing ASK offer abortion validation in Turbo mode
reason: Turbo-mode abort status is updated on a memory copy, so the origin offer stays live and the attacker can extract collateral/protocol funds.

title: H-14. Missing check for aborted origin offer allows bid takers to relist unbacked offers
reason: An aborted origin offer can be relisted unbacked, so later takers' deposits compensate the relister.

title: H-10. [H-4] The function `PreMarkets::listOffer` charges an incorrect collateral amount, allowing users to manipulating collateral rates and drain the protocol's funds
reason: listOffer charges collateral at the old rate but records the new (higher) rate, so closing refunds more than deposited and drains the protocol.

title: H-11. listOffer maker can settle offer via settleAskMaker() in Turbo settle type.
reason: In Turbo mode a relisted sub-offer owner calls settleAskMaker and is paid out of the original maker's shared collateral.

title: H-01. Incorrect set up and logic of `referralInfoMap` in `SystemConfig::updateReferrerInfo` function
reason: Anyone can write referralInfoMap entries, register themselves as referrer and capture fees meant for the real referrer.

title: [C04] Rogue borrower can manipulate other account’s borrow balance
reason: C04: a rogue borrower can shift debt onto another account's borrow balance, avoiding their own obligation.

title: Lack of access controls in updateReserveTotalBorrowsByRateMode
reason: updateReserveTotalBorrowsByRateMode has no access control; anyone can rewrite a victim's debt and liquidate the position.

title: [C01] Users can steal funds
reason: C01: accounting bug lets a user withdraw/transfer more than deposited, moving pool funds to the attacker.

title: redeem does not properly validate parameters and allows drainage of
reason: redeem trusts the caller-supplied aToken for underlying/balance, so a fake aToken reporting a huge balance is paid real underlying.

title: [C02] Borrowers can avoid liquidation
reason: C02: borrower can avoid liquidation and keep the borrowed value, leaving bad debt to the pool.

title: [H03] Deactivated collateral reserve can be used in liquidation
reason: H03: only the debt reserve is checked with onlyActiveReserve, so a liquidator can seize a collateral reserve the admin deactivated.

title: Lack of access control for FeeProvider setter functions
reason: FeeProvider setters have no access control, so anyone can redirect all origination fees to themselves and raise the fee rate.

title: Wrong reserve ratio returned by getReserveRatio when constrained
reason: getReserveRatio returns a wrong value when constrained; mispricing is plausible but the released text does not establish a direct attacker payout.

title: Max profit can exceed amount reserved from vault
reason: A position whose max profit exceeds the reserved vault amount pays out more than reserved when it wins, leaving bad debt the trader keeps.

title: Unsafe cast in take profit can lead to fund loss
reason: Take-profit set to uint256.max casts to -1 and books a ~900% profit on close, paying the trader from the vault.

title: Partial trades update open-interest incorrectly
reason: Partial trades update open interest incorrectly, so funding and OI limits understate the real position and the trader avoids funding costs.

title: Locked shares have undue access to historical rewards
reason: lastSharePoint is left at 0 on lock, so the position is credited historical rewards and later claimants are underfunded.

title: Update margin uses new leverage for balance release
reason: Margin update uses the new leverage to compute the released balance, releasing more collateral than entitled.

title: Precision loss in totalLockPoints causes undue rewards and insolvency
reason: Precision loss in totalLockPoints inflates rewards per lock point, overpaying claimers and rendering the reward pool insolvent.

title: Composable pools can be calculated incorrectly
reason: Composable BPT is valued as min token USD price times pool rate, overvaluing BPT so the attacker borrows against it.

title: _exchangerate can be manipulated, leading to inflation attack
reason: _exchangeRate can be set by a minimal first deposit, so later depositors get zero/unfair LP tokens and the attacker withdraws their deposits.

title: Oracle manipulation via missing balancer vault read-only reentrancy check
reason: Read-only reentrancy during Balancer join/exit gives BPTOracle a wrong BPT price, letting the attacker borrow/withdraw against inflated collateral.

title: Drain the rewards in the protocol
reason: Any Aura LP holder can claim Omnipool rewards they are not entitled to, draining the reward pool.

title: lastweightupdate mapping in omnipoolcontroller.sol will always be 0
reason: lastWeightUpdate mapping always reads 0, changing weight-update timing; the released text does not establish a direct payout to the caller.

title: Theft of rewards via sandwich attack
reason: Reward-claim swap has no slippage limit, so a searcher sandwiches the claim and captures the user's rewards.

title: Ineffective slippage control
reason: Deposit liquidity is derived from token_max_a at spot, so a sandwich forces the depositor to supply mostly token A for far less LP and the attacker captures the difference.

title: Attackers will steal the reserve from the `Vault` by receiving `ra` in `FlashSwapRouter::__swapDsforRa()`
reason: swapRaforDs -> __swapDsforRa -> __afterFlashswapSell sends Ra to msg.sender while the Vault is funded from its existing balance.

title: Lack of slippage protection leads to loss of protocol funds
reason: Unslippaged swap lets a searcher back-run and capture the difference from protocol funds.

title: Attackers will steal the reserve from the Vault by receiving ra in FlashSwa pRouter::__swapDsforRa()
reason: __swapDsforRa flash-swaps and then funds the Vault from its existing Ra instead of the swap proceeds, so the caller receives the reserve.

title: Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry
reason: Early redemption withdraws Ra without decrementing the locked amount, so the user can withdraw again after expiry and receive more than deposited.

title: Users redeeming early will with- draw Ra without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry
reason: Duplicate of the early-redemption finding: Ra withdrawn without reducing the lock, then withdrawn again after expiry.

title: Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to VaultPoolLib::rede em() not always decreasing self.withdraw alPool.raBalance and self.withdrawalPoo l.paBalance
reason: Duplicate of the VaultPoolLib.redeem finding: balances not decremented, reserves double-counted, inflated shares redeemed.

title: Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `self.withdrawalPool.raBalance` and `self.withdrawalPool.paBalance`
reason: redeem does not always decrease withdrawalPool.raBalance/paBalance, so the next issuance double-counts reserves, inflates exchange rates and redeeming shares drains the vault.

title: Attack to make `CurveSubject` to be a `HoneyPot`
reason: Creator points referralFeeDestination at a reverting contract so sells fail while buys work, then restores it and dumps at the inflated price.

title: Malformed equate statement
reason: Duplicate of the malformed-equate finding: access checks do not revert, enabling privileged calls by any EOA.

title: Unrestricted claiming of fees due to missing balance updates in FeeSplitter
reason: userFeeOffset is only updated on buys/sells, so tokens transferred to a fresh address with offset 0 can claim historical fees; rotating tokens repeats the claim.

title: Malformed equate statement
reason: Malformed equate in Security.sol modifiers makes onlyOwner/onlyManager no-ops, so anyone can call owner-only fee/mint/fund functions.

title: Unauthorized Access to setCurves Function
reason: setCurves has no access control; a malicious curves contract reports inflated balances and FeeSplitter pays out on the spoofed numbers.

title: Unrestricted claiming of fees due to missing balance updates in `FeeSplitter`
reason: FeeSplitter does not update balances on transfer, so fees can be claimed without entitlement.

title: Unauthorized Access to `setCurves` Function
reason: Duplicate of the setCurves access-control finding: anyone can set the curves contract and trade the manipulated curve.

title: MarginTrading.sol: Missing flash loan initiator check allows attacker to open trades, close trades and steal funds
reason: Missing flash-loan initiator check lets anyone invoke the callback and open/close trades with pool funds, then withdraw the proceeds.

title: A user can get more dTokens than they should get via D3VaultFunding.userDeposit(), due to accounting issues in D3VaultLiquidation.liquidate()
reason: Stale balance after liquidate() lets a depositor mint more dTokens than entitled via D3VaultFunding.userDeposit.

title: User can perform sandwich attack on withdrawReserves for profit
reason: Deposit before withdrawReserves and withdraw after it, capturing the reserve-driven exchange-rate change at the protocol's expense.

title: Pool can be drained if there are no LP_FEES
reason: With no LP_FEES the GSP accounting lets a user withdraw the pool's reserves.

title: When a D3MM pool repays all of the borrowed funds to vault using D3Funding.sol repayAll, an attacker can steal double the amount of those funds from vault
reason: poolRepayAll subtracts instead of adding to info.balance, creating a phantom balance the attacker deposits against and withdraws, stealing double the repayment.

title: User can perform sandwich attack on with- drawReserves for profit
reason: Duplicate sandwich-on-withdrawReserves finding: searcher deposits before and withdraws after the reserve withdrawal.

title: Anyone can sell other users' tokens as fromToken, and get the toToken's themselves due to decodeData.payer is never checked.
reason: decodeData.payer is never checked, so a caller can sell another user's approved tokens and receive the output token.

title: DEPOSITING ON ANY POOL USING ANY TOKEN
reason: Depositing any pool with any token is accepted; the released text does not establish the mispricing direction or a concrete payout.

title: DEPOSITING TO ANY POOL/TOKEN WITH ANY AMOUNT VIA CONTROLLED POLICY CENTER
reason: Anyone can deposit any pool/token/amount through the policy center, bypassing policy limits and diluting or extracting pool value.

title: POOL INCOMES ON REPORTER REWARD CAN BE ARBITRARILY INCREASED
reason: premiumIncome can be called by anyone to inflate pool income, and the reporter reward computed from it drains SHD from Treasury.

title: PUBLICLY EXPOSED FUNCTIONS
reason: Unpermissioned addToken/addPool/updateWeight let an attacker add a worthless token with huge weight and farm the pool's rewards.

title: INVALID PERCENTAGE RESULTS IN LESS PAYED DEBT
reason: payDebt computes amount*80/10000 (0.8%) instead of 80%, so the caller pays ~100x less than owed and keeps the difference.

title: AN ATTACKER CAN WITHDRAW NOT OWNED TOKENS AND STEAL FUNDS
reason: Public withdraw accepts an arbitrary token and amount and transfers it to the caller without checking pool ownership, draining every ERC-20 the pool holds.

title: UPDATING THE 0 INDEX TOKEN WEIGHT VIA UNREGISTERED TOKENS
reason: updateWeight derives the index from _getIndex, so an unregistered token updates index 0 (and a zero weight is accepted), reweighting rewards to the attacker.

title: Closing a Position Can Create an In inite Bad Debt
reason: Duplicate infinite-bad-debt finding: the closing trader walks away with value while the protocol absorbs the loss.

title: PnL Can Be Artificially Lowered by Manipulating the AMM Price
reason: AMM price manipulation lowers reported PnL, reducing what the trader owes or increasing what they receive.

title: PnL Can Be Arti icially Lowered by Manipulating the AMM Price
reason: Duplicate PnL-manipulation finding: manipulated AMM price lets the trader avoid losses or liquidate at the wrong PnL.

title: PnL Avoidance Through Zero Exposure Exploit
reason: Offsetting long/short makes positionValue 0, calcHypotheticalMR returns only MMR and ignores negative PnL, so the trader withdraws all collateral and leaves the loss as bad debt.

title: A Liquidator Can Liquidate a Position With Infinitely Bad Price
reason: Manipulating liquidity size to match the liquidation size yields an almost infinite price; the liquidator repays a tiny debt and takes the whole collateral.

title: A Liquidator Can Liquidate a Position With In initely Bad Price
reason: Duplicate of the infinitely-bad-price liquidation finding.

title: Closing a Position Can Create an Infinite Bad Debt
reason: Closing a short against a pool drained to near the position size produces a near-infinite average price, booking unbounded bad debt while the attacker's LP position withdraws the excess.

title: Reentrancy in distributePremium allows attacker to bypass system limits, invariants and manipulate FSD token price
reason: Refund callback re-enters purchaseMembership before state updates, bypassing wallet/CSB caps and minting FSD at a stale price.

title: `Withdrawable.withdraw` does not decrease `pendingWithdrawals`
reason: withdraw does not decrease pendingWithdrawals, so the same withdrawal can be repeated.

title: User can bypass copay and get 100% cover- age
reason: The cost-share check is applied to the wrong quantity, so a claim is opened with 100% coverage while only the minimum copay is paid.

title: Locked funds from tokenization are credited twice to user leading to protocol fund loss
reason: Locked funds are released twice when conviction is re-acquired from an NFT, crediting the user twice at protocol expense.

title: Free CSB and bypass of maximum CSB per wallet by toping up/renewing while opening a cost share request
reason: Opening a cost-share request then topping up/renewing bypasses the CSB deduction and the per-wallet cap.

title: Anyone Can Arbitrarily Call `FSDVesting.updateVestedTokens()`
reason: updateVestedTokens has no access control, so a beneficiary can inflate the vested amount and claim it.

title: ERC20ConvictionScore._writeCheckpoint` does not write to storage on same block
reason: _writeCheckpoint does not write on the same block; the released text does not establish a concrete value transfer.

title: [H02] Outdated oracle prices being used throughout the protocol
reason: Protocol operations use an outdated oracle price, so the attacker trades against it (buys underpriced / sells overpriced).

title: [H03] Inconsistent use of oracles
reason: Two oracle paths disagree, so a round trip between operations priced by different oracles extracts the spread.

title: [C01] Protocol does not support token decimals
reason: Tokens with non-18 decimals are mispriced because the protocol assumes 18, and the difference is extractable.

title: [C03] Anyone can partially bypass the FEI sell penalty to earn a profit
reason: Buying FEI for the incentive and selling back in many small sells keeps the quadratic penalty below the incentive, so the attacker profits repeatedly.

title: [C01] Anyone can steal all the TRIBE tokens from the reward pool
reason: Burning LP via burnFrom collapses the reward denominator to 1, so a second account claims the pool's entire TRIBE rewardBalance.

title: [C05] Anyone with enough liquidity to reach the maxGenesisPrice can make profit from genesis
reason: Depositing enough ETH to reach maxGenesisPrice lets the attacker profit from the genesis pricing mechanism.

title: [H02] Introduction of additional BondingCurves creates period of volatility
reason: Each new bonding curve sells FEI at a 0-5% discount, so bots buy the discount and immediately sell on-market for a profit.

title: updateBalances Should Be Called Before collectFees()
reason: updateBalances is called after collectFees, so fee accounting is wrong; the released text does not establish who captures the difference.

title: Position Might Still Be Liquiditable Even When User Increases Position
reason: Fees charged during increasePosition can push a position under the threshold, letting a liquidator close it for the incentive.

title: Liquidation is not validated at the right time.
reason: increasePosition validates health before applying the update, so an unhealthy position beyond the leverage limit is accepted and the extra exposure can be closed at protocol expense.

title: Collateral is reduced twice when a position is liquidated by a user different from
reason: Third-party liquidation reduces the position's collateral twice, and the liquidator/borrower captures the double deduction.

title: Anyone can set a malicious `diamond` address.
reason: Anyone can set the diamond address used by the onlyDiamond modifier, point it at a malicious implementation and take the proxy's funds.

title: Referrer is not valid for earning for more time than expected.
reason: maxDaysForEarning is multiplied by 24 hours twice, so a referrer earns for ~24x the intended window and over-claims referral rewards.

title: The minimum time for earning as a referrer can be bypassed resulting in user claiming
reason: The minimum earning time for a referrer can be bypassed, so a user claims referral rewards without serving the period.

title: minIn checks can be bypassed via different routes
reason: minIn is compared against a balance that already includes idle funds/fees, so the slippage guard can be bypassed and liquidity added at a manipulated ratio that the attacker arbitrages.

title: First depositor can break the reward calculation within the MultiFeeDistribution contract
reason: First depositor breaks MultiFeeDistribution reward accounting and captures rewards owed to later stakers.

title: Contract can be drained via sophisticated mandate bypass mechanism
reason: Crafted call satisfies the mandate checks but routes funds outside the allowed strategy set, releasing reserves to the attacker's contract.

title: Share inflation attack possibility for first depositor
reason: First depositor donates to inflate the share-price divisor, later depositors round to zero shares, and the attacker redeems their assets.

title: Edge-case during directDeposit state allows for thefting from a vault
reason: Edge case in the directDeposit state lets a depositor take assets that belong to the vault.

title: Ratio enforcement can be abused to frontrun depositors resulting in a loss of tokens for depositors
reason: Ratio enforcement can be front-run so depositors lose tokens to the attacker.

title: Raw MEV possibility via compound/rebalance
reason: Compound/rebalance can be sandwiched for raw MEV at the vault's expense.

title: Missing access control on update() function in Earning.sol opens up many attack vectors
reason: update() is callable by anyone and can mint Earning/rewrite Fs for an arbitrary account; released text frames it as trust-score manipulation, not a demonstrated cash-out.

title: During voting the attacker's refund is vulnerable to a sandwich attack
reason: The refund swap in _tryFinalize has no slippage bound, so a searcher can sandwich it and capture the refund value.

title: Anyone can steal protocol's llido assets and ether balance using its distributive functions
reason: claimRevenueShareDevTeam/earningPulls are public and pay address(this).balance and LLido reserves to msg.sender, so any EOA can sweep the contract.

title: _updatesponsor implementation contradicts sponsor role in pool and open's backrunning attack vectors
reason: Backrunning a stake with a marginally larger stake wins the trustor slot and its sponsor rewards.

title: Attacker can take advantage of multiplier when there's only one second left, allowing them to fraudulently gain voting power
reason: Staking a large amount for the last second of an existing lock mints full multiplier voting power, letting the attacker win votes and capture Geth rewards.

title: Malicious poolowner can withdraw earnings without affecting trust score

reason: Any LP can call IndexTemplate.resume() on a locked PayingOut pool and exit before compensation, shifting the loss to remaining LPs.

title: Bypassing Quarantine and Reusing the Same Report Allows Minting Uncollateralized stETH

title: Fee Payment Underflow Inflates Vault TotalValue
reason: Fees > value plus a direct ETH gift makes totalValue - fees underflow to 2^256-1, and the owner mints stETH against it.

title: DineroWithdrawRequestManager vulnera- ble to token overwithdrawal via batch ID overlap
reason: Batch IDs overlap between requests and _finalizeWithdrawImpl redeems every upxETH balance in the range, so one request can claim another's tokens.

title: Missing Slippage Protection in Expired PT Redemption Causes User Fund Loss
reason: redeemExpiredPT calls sy.redeem with minTokenOut=0, so a searcher can sandwich the redemption and take the slippage.

title: `DineroWithdrawRequestManager` vulnerable to token overwithdrawal via batch ID overlap
reason: Overlapping batch IDs let a request redeem upxETH outside its own batch range, over-withdrawing the manager.

title: Incorrect assumption that one (1) Pendle Standard Yield (SY) token is equal to one (1) Yield To- ken when computing the price in the oracle
reason: Treating 1 SY as 1 yield token overvalues PT collateral when useSyOracleRate is on, letting a borrower mint/borrow against inflated value.

title: Attacker can drain the entire suppliers on Morpho market by inflating collateral price
reason: initiateWithdraw escrows shares without burning them, so the attacker donates yield tokens to inflate price() and borrows against the inflated Morpho collateral while keeping the withdrawal claim.

title: Malicious user can change the `TradeType` to steal funds from the vault or withdraw request manager

title: lastweightupdate mapping in omnipoolcontroller.sol will always be 0

title: The bptpricestablepool() function of bptoracle.sol contract calculates the value of stable bpt incorrectly
reason: Stable-pool BPT valuation ignores per-token rates, so the oracle can over/under-value the pool; no concrete extraction path is shown.

title: Bptoracle.bptpriceweightpool() tries to use totalsupply() to get the total supply of the pools, resulting in inaccurate bptprice
reason: BPTOracle uses totalSupply() on pools that need getActualSupply, mispricing BPT used for withdrawals/TVL; released text does not quantify an attacker gain.

title: _exchangerate can be manipulated, leading to inﬂation attack Submitted by 0xTheBlackPanther, also found by J4X98, Chad0, golu and Victor Okafor
reason: deposit() derives the exchange rate from the pool's own balances, so an attacker deposits 2 wei, sets the rate, lets victims mint zero LP, then withdraws the pool.

title: Drain the rewards in the protocol
reason: getUserTotalDeposit values any Balancer/Aura BPT balance, so a non-depositor can claim from the reward pool and deplete it.

title: Theft of rewards via sandwich attack
reason: swapForGem does a Balancer batchSwap with max limits and no slippage bound, so a searcher can sandwich claimEarnings and take the rewards.

title: Drain Rewards of anyone using overrideReceiver() and removeOverrideAddress()
reason: overrideReceiver lets any caller set a victim as override, and removeOverrideAddress migrates the victim's whole unclaimed balance to the caller.

title: Excess bid amount refund mechanism is redundant and makes it possible to steal all funds from BidderRegistry
reason: When availableAmount is 0, openBid refunds the full bid from the registry's balance, so a zero-deposit bidder can set bid=TVL and be paid out.

title: BidderRegistry can be drained by reentering BidderRegistry::openBid()

title: Shared secret can be altered to farm a bid multiple times

title: Excess bid amount refund mechanism is redundant and makes it possible to steal all funds from BidderRegistry

title: BidderRegistry can be drained by reentering BidderRegistry::openBid()
reason: openBid calls the bidder before writing bidState, so a malicious bidder can reenter and be paid repeatedly.

title: Overpayment to Bidder in Slash Function Due to Incorrect Amount Transfer
reason: slash sends the full amt instead of residualAmt to the bidder, overpaying the bidder from provider stake.

title: tradingFunction returns wrong invariant at bounds, allowing to steal all pool reserves
reason: At the invariant bounds the probit term is skipped and set to 0, so draining the reserve does not decrease the invariant and the swap is accepted.

title: Swaps can be done for free and steal the reserve given large liquidity allocation
reason: With liquidity >2^126, deltaOutput.divWadDown(liquidity) rounds to 0, so a swap with 1 wei input passes the invariant check and credits the whole reserve.

title: Transfer operations may silently fail due to the lack of contract existence
reason: A token address with no code makes safeTransfer succeed silently, which could credit a deposit without funds; the released body is withheld so no concrete cash-out is shown.

title: [C02] Issued options might not be backed by underlying assets
reason: close() uses > instead of >= for expiry, so at the expiry second option tokens are not burned and the writer can extract underlying and resell the options.

title: [C01] Anyone can steal funds from the Option contract before they are used
reason: take() is external with no access control and sweeps the difference between actual and cached balances plus option/redeem tokens.

title: Unsafe type-casting
reason: getNetBalance downcasts physical/internal balances; an internal balance above int256.max wraps negative and settlement credits the attacker the physical balance without payment.

title: [C03] Deposited funds can be stolen or lost due to transaction ordering
reason: Deposits are pooled without per-user accounting, so a miner/attacker can order deposits before a mint and receive all option/redeem tokens.

title: Rounding error allows liquidity to be added without depositing tokens
reason: Rounding lets addLiquidity mint LP shares without depositing the matching tokens, diluting existing reserves.

title: Risk of token theft due to possible integer underflow in slt
reason: Title reports a possible slt underflow enabling token theft, but the body is withheld and no path is established.

title: Swap function returns incorrectly scaled output token amount
reason: Swap output is scaled with the wrong decimals; direction and profit are not established in the withheld body.

title: Pool strike price could be zero due to lack of lower bound check on

title: Attackers can steal funds by swapping in both directions

title: Risk of token theft due to unchecked type conversion
reason: Title reports token theft via unchecked type conversion; body withheld, so the path is not established.

title: Incorrect access control and entry point implementation
reason: SetVault and MockIReceive are callable by anyone, so the attacker can point the gateway at their vault or mint arbitrary ROUTE.

title: Attackers can register and deregister their accounts for profit
reason: register costs 1 yoctoNEAR but storage_unregister refunds 1.25e21 yoctoNEAR, so looping register/unregister pays out storage deposits.

title: HandlerExecMsg::IReceive message is sent to the handler contract regardless of the ASM contract execution result
reason: The ASM Verify result is ignored, so an unauthorized iReceive is executed and can mint/route ROUTE.

title: Updating the forwarder's claimable amount during a withdrawal request uses the wrong decimal precision, resulting in the ability to steal funds
reason: update_claimable_amount rescales an already-scaled amount, so the claimable deduction is 10^12 too small and the attacker can claim the surplus.

title: Attackers can steal funds by repeatedly withdrawing blocked funds
reason: BLOCKED_FUNDS is never decremented, so a depositor can withdraw the same blocked amount repeatedly from other depositors' funds.

title: Erroneous claimable updates lead to the loss of the forwarder's funds
reason: update_chain_liquidty_and_claimable_amount overwrites instead of adding, so a forwarder's claimable amount is misstated and can be over-claimed.

title: Failed iAck messages can be replayed
reason: Failed iAck does not set ACK_ACCEPTED, so the ack can be replayed; the released text does not show a value transfer.

title: DarkPoolAssetManager can be drained by looping over join(), joinSplit() or swap() with only some initial amount
reason: join/joinSplit/swap do not check that the two notes differ, so the same note doubles the spendable amount and a loop drains the manager.

title: In StakingAssetManager::lockERC20() the resulting note is created with asset instead of zkToken
reason: lockERC20 builds the note with asset instead of zkToken; the note cannot be unlocked, so funds are locked rather than stolen.

title: UniswapLiquidityAssetManager::_validateCollectFeesArgs() validates nullifier instead of note footer
reason: _validateCollectFeesArgs checks nullifiers instead of note footers, so the same footer can be reused to collect fees repeatedly.

title: Checks-effects-interations pattern is not always followed, which can be used to drain all tokens
reason: withdrawETH sends ETH before _postWithdraw, so the receive hook can reuse the still-unused nullifier and double-withdraw in a loop.

title: Curve multi exchange does not validate assetIn and assetOut against route
reason: assetIn/assetOut are not checked against route, so the caller can name a valuable assetOut while the route swaps a fake coin.

title: MerkleRoot is not validated in all StakingAssetManager functions
reason: Merkle root is not validated, so an attacker can supply a forged root containing a fake note and redeem all assets.

title: _addLiquidity() slippage is incorrectly set
reason: _addLiquidity computes mintAmount after the swap and applies a hardcoded 95%, so the deposit can be sandwiched.

title: liquidatePositionsPartyB can be used by malicious liquidator to liquidate only select positions which artificially inflates partyA upnl and allows to steal funds

title: LibMuon Signature hash collision

reason: Capping partyB loss at its current allocated balance during partyA liquidation lets partyB end with an inflated balance at protocol expense.

title: PartyA and PartyB nonce is not incremented in any of the liquidation functions which can lead to all protocol funds being stolen in some cases

title: CLGauge stakers can earn more than their due, with claimable rewards exceeding available rewards
reason: CLGauge._earned retroactively applies prior-epoch rewards, so a staker can claim more than the gauge holds.

title: CLGauge.deposit() doesn't verify that the liquidity to stake is from the pool the gauge integrates with
reason: CLGauge.deposit accepts an NFT from any pool, so a fake CLPool position earns gauge emissions meant for the integrated pool.

title: Inflated voting balance due to duplicated veNFTs within a checkpoint

title: Voting overwrites `checkpoint.voted` in last checkpoint, so users can just vote right before claiming rewards

title: Liquidity staked at ticks can be manipulated to impact swap fees and rewards

title: Users can mint DUSD with less collateral than required, which gives them free DUSD and may open a liquidatable position

title: Attacker can profit from discount fees

title: DUSD assets can be minted with less ETH collateral than required

title: Liquidation doesn’t account for penalty when calculating collateral to give, allowing users to profit by borrowing and self-liquidating

title: CDPVault.sol#liquidatePositionBadDebt() doesn’t correctly handle profit and loss
reason: Bad-debt liquidation mis-splits profit/loss between CDPVault and PoolV3, over-crediting the liquidator at LP expense.

title: AuraVault::claim reward calculation does not deduct fees from reward amount, causing DoS or extra rewards lost
reason: The fee is not deducted, so the caller receives the full reward amount and either over-draws the contract (DoS) or takes other users' rewards.

title: Liquidation doesn't account for penalty when calculating collateral to give, allowing users to profit by borrowing and self-liquidating
reason: Same penalty omission: borrow to the limit, self-liquidate, and keep collateral worth more than the debt extinguished.

title: Zero rates on new quoted tokens allow an attacker to take an interest free quota

title: InfernalRiftBelow.claimRoyalties no verification msg.sender
reason: claimRoyalties trusts xDomainMessageSender without restricting msg.sender to the official messenger, so any contract can spoof the sender and take bridged assets.

title: Donation fees are sandwichable in one transaction
reason: Donations have no per-block cap and use the current tick, so JIT liquidity around donate() captures the donation.

title: Owner Can Lose The Token After Being Unlocked but Not Withdrawn

title: Protected listings checkpoints are not always updated when the total supply changes

title: Quorum overflow in CollectionShutdown leads to complete drain of contract's funds
reason: quorumVotes cast to uint88 can wrap to a small value and claims divide by it, letting a claimant withdraw far more than entitled.

reason: Swaps execute without a min-out, so a searcher sandwiches them and captures the price impact.

reason: An unscaled oracle price misprices collateral, but the released text does not establish which actor gains or how the mispricing is monetised.

title: Malicious actors can exploit user-approved allowances on VaultRouter to drain their ERC4626 tokens
reason: VaultRouter accepts an arbitrary owner, so anyone can redeem a victim's approved vault shares to themselves.

title: The implementation of pullTokensWithPermit poses a risk, allowing malicious actors to steal tokens
reason: pullTokensWithPermit does not authenticate the flow, so an attacker can front-run the permit and sweep the pulled tokens.

title: ElixirStrategy wrong withdrawal accounting allows undercollateralized borrowing
reason: withdrawnAmount is computed with balanceBefore=0 so pre-existing holdings count as yield, inflating registry collateral and permitting over-borrow.

title: Cross contract reentrancy during ElixirStrategy.withdraw() swaps allows an attacker to double account collateral
reason: Re-entering during the multihop swap deposits tokenIn that the balance-delta accounting double counts as yield.

title: Partial withdrawals don't work with Elixir strategy
reason: Cooling all shares then withdrawing 1 wei makes the whole cooled amount register as yield, doubling recorded collateral that can be borrowed against.

title: LiquidationManager::liquidate() allows liquidators to get liquidation bonus and leave bad debt behind
reason: The liquidator takes the bonus while the shortfall is left on the protocol, a direct transfer to the liquidator.

title: If jUSD depegs, it will get in a death spiral

title: Misplaced liquidatable check allows healthy positions to be liquidated
reason: A misplaced check lets a liquidator seize collateral from a healthy position and collect the bonus.

title: Limit Orders Can Be Incorrectly Filled
reason: A partially crossed order is marked filled and deleted; the release text shows maker loss but not an attacker payout.

title: Integer Underflow in _getTargetOutput Due to Improper Type Casting
reason: A negative int128 cast to uint128 bypasses the penalty, but the released text does not establish a positive attacker gain.

title: Sandwich Attack Possible via JIT Attack in AntiSandwichHook
reason: A JIT LP concentrated at the donation tick receives most of the penalty donation paid by the sandwiched swap.

title: Accrued Limit Order Fees Can Be Stolen
reason: Fees accrued over an order's life are split pro-rata at fill time, so an attacker adds a large liquidity share just before the fill and withdraws after.

title: Incorrect Unspecified Amount Handling Breaks Anti-Sandwich Logic
reason: The anti-sandwich penalty can be bypassed, but the release text does not tie that to a concrete extraction path.

title: Incorrect Timing of removingAllLiquidity Flag Calculation in cancelOrder
reason: The flag is evaluated after liquidityTotal is decremented, so the last LP forfeits fees and a later caller can reuse the order key to claim them.

title: Player can mint more fighter NFTs during claim of rewards by leveraging reentrancy on the `claimRewards() function`
reason: Re-entering claimRewards before state updates mints more fighter NFTs than allowed.

title: Players have complete freedom to customize the fighter NFT when calling `redeemMintPass` and can redeem fighters of types Dendroid and with rare attributes
reason: redeemMintPass lets the caller choose fighter type and attributes, minting rare NFTs for the price of a common mint pass.

title: Since you can reroll with a different fighterType than the NFT you own, you can reroll bypassing maxRerollsAllowed and reroll attributes based on a different fighterType
reason: Rerolling with a different fighterType bypasses maxRerollsAllowed and lets the attacker re-roll into better attributes.

title: Malicious user can stake an amount which causes zero curStakeAtRisk on a loss but equal rewardPoints to a fair user on a win
reason: A stake sized so curStakeAtRisk rounds to zero keeps rewardPoints while risking nothing.

title: Player can mint more fighter NFTs during claim of rewards by leveraging reentrancy on the claimRewards() function
reason: Re-entering claimRewards before state updates mints extra fighter NFTs to the attacker.

title: Malicious user can stake an amount which causes zero curStakeAtRisk on a loss but equal rewardPoints to a fair user on a win
reason: Staking 1 wei makes curStakeAtRisk round to zero while still earning reward points, so the attacker risks nothing for real rewards.

title: Supply principal is manipulable by anyone
reason: Anyone can deposit another AAVE-supported token to reset supplyPrincipal and flip hasBeenLiquidated; the text shows corruption of the interest index but not a clean attacker payout.

title: transferFrom does not lower the allowance
reason: The allowance is never decremented, so an approved spender can repeatedly transferFrom up to the victim's whole balance.

title: migrationFee increases borrow without considering availableBorrow in GroomableManager
reason: The migration fee is added to debt without checking availableBorrow, letting a borrower exceed the borrow limit.

title: User harvest and vault reserves are counted twice when calling storeCommitCalculation
reason: HarvestHelper returns updated reserves and the caller adds them again, so a user can withdraw more than entitled.

title: Repeated calls draining all funds from strategies in Far mBufferDispatcher
reason: Repeated dispatcher calls withdraw from strategies without decrementing the accounting variable, so the caller drains strategy funds.

title: Anyone can steal all funds of a vault which has this strategy registered
reason: A missing access check on the registered strategy lets any caller drain the vault's funds.

title: MEV Extractable From distribute() Function
reason: Staking immediately before distribute() and withdrawing after captures a disproportionate share of the period's rewards.

title: addStrategy() Is Publicly Accessible
reason: Anyone can register a strategy and redirect credit-token mint/burn destinations, taking the credit accounting.

title: (Re-Audit) Users May Supply Arbitrary Collateral Contrary to Specification
reason: Arbitrary collateral can be supplied, so worthless tokens back real borrowing from the pool.

title: Credit Tokens Burned From the Wrong Account
reason: Burning credit tokens from the wrong account shifts debt/credit between users, leaving the attacker with a reduced obligation.

title: _repayCredit() Is Publicly Accessible
reason: The internal repay path is callable without repayCredit's checks; the release text does not show whether the caller gains or only forces/griefs a repayment.

title: Protocol May Use Incorrect Prices
reason: A single oracle with no staleness or zero checks lets an attacker borrow or liquidate against a manipulated price.

title: Arbitrary CPI
reason: An unchecked CPI accepts an attacker-supplied program, redirecting token transfers to the attacker.

title: Users can potentially create offers without paying USDC
reason: An offer can be created without escrowing the promised USDC, so a seller who accepts hands over the NFT unpaid.

title: Attackers can steal funds in the vault in migrate_token.rs:migrate_token
reason: migrate_token does not bind the vault/authority, so an attacker supplies their own accounts and moves the vault's tokens.

title: All funds in vault_account_program can be drained
reason: The vault account program's authority is not validated, allowing any caller to drain it.

title: User can stake arbitrary token to get rewards
reason: Any token can be staked while still earning rewards, so the attacker stakes worthless tokens and drains the reward pool.

title: Attackers can steal funds in the vault in buy.rs:buy
reason: The buy instruction does not bind the vault correctly, so an attacker passes their own accounts and takes vault funds.

title: `Funds.sechi` is never updated, leading to reused secrets
reason: A counterparty who has seen a secret can claim a new HTLC immediately and take the locked principal.

title: Reentrancy attack on `Loans.pull` can lead to draining funds
reason: The loan's off flag is set last, so a transfer callback re-enters pull and repeats the principal/fee payout.

title: Reentrancy attack on `Funds.pull` can lead to draining funds
reason: An ERC223/ERC777 transfer callback re-enters pull before the balance is decremented, draining the Funds contract.

title: `Sales.take` transfers too little to the lender (and too much to the borrower)
reason: The borrower receives the difference between the sale proceeds and the underpaid lender amount.

title: `Loans.unpay` can be called repeatedly to drain tokens
reason: Each unpay call pays out without clearing loan state, so repeated calls drain the loan escrow.

title: Reentrancy attack on `Sales.take` can lead to draining funds
reason: A token transfer callback re-enters take() before taken(sale) is set, repeating payouts until the Sales contract is drained.

title: Contract is drainable due to bypassing “in-range-check” with onPositionUse hook
reason: The hook bypasses the in-range check, so a double-sided option is minted as if single-sided and its mispriced value is extracted.

title: Strike price calculation is incorrect in case pair is inverse, impacting premium calculation
reason: On an inverse pair the strike maps below spot, so the attacker mints an option at a favourable strike/premium and exercises it for risk-free profit.

title: Contract is drainable due to incorrect “in-range-check”
reason: Truncation makes a double-sided position look single-sided, so settle() swaps more value than was paid in and drains the market.

title: In-range validation within mintOption is based on _params.tickLower/Upper instead of opTick.tickLower/Upper
reason: The check validates the wrong tick fields, so an attacker supplies params that pass while opTick sits on the other side of spot.

title: Profit can be stolen due to lack of optionId validation
reason: An unvalidated optionId lets the caller claim profit belonging to another option position.

title: Frontrun of settlement with a swap allows for tricking settler into unexpected call-path
reason: A front-run swap moves the pool price so the settler executes at a skewed price and the searcher captures the difference.

title: [C01] All CASH tokens approved to Augur can be emptied
reason: trustedTransfer pulls the victim's CASH approval into an attacker-controlled market; the attacker then controls that market (chained with C02).

title: [C02] CASH tokens can be stolen from the Market contract
reason: Attacker sets a malicious universe, initializes the market as owner/repBondOwner and moves all CASH held by the Market to themselves.

title: Update: [H06] Legacy REP tokens can be migrated to child universes
reason: Legacy REP can be credited into child universes, bypassing the fork's use-or-lose forfeiture and preserving value for the migrator.

title: [H03] Affiliate keys can be stolen
reason: Signature is not bound to msg.sender, so a pending addKey signature can be hijacked to register a KYC key to the attacker, but the report establishes KYC bypass and affiliate credit, not a fund transfer.

title: [H04] Reentrancy vulnerabilities in Market contract
reason: Report states neither reentrancy is exploitable in the deployed state because the Market holds only the repBond; draining returns the attacker's own bond, so no clear external gain.

title: [C01] Anyone can register backdoored wallets for any owner in GnosisSafeRegistry contract
reason: Anyone can register a proxy safe under a victim owner; funds later sent to that owner through the registry lookup land in the attacker's backdoored safe.

title: Arbitrary transactions possible due to insufficient signature validation
reason: Insufficient signature validation lets an attacker submit arbitrary transactions executed by the smart wallet.

title: Paymaster ETH can be drained with malicious sender
reason: A malicious sender replays a paymaster signature to keep consuming the paymaster's deposit until it is empty.

title: Attacker can gain control of counterfactual wallet
reason: Attacker deploys the victim's counterfactual wallet with an attacker-chosen handler before the owner and then drains the pre-funded address.

title: `FeeRefund.tokenGasPriceFactor` is not included in signed transaction data allowing the submitter to steal funds
reason: The unsigned tokenGasPriceFactor lets the submitter inflate the ERC20 gas refund and take the difference from the wallet.

title: Theft of funds under relaying the transaction
reason: Relayed transaction accounting lets the relayer over-claim the gas refund and take funds from the wallet.

title: Replay attack (EIP712 signed transaction)
reason: A signed EIP-712 transaction can be replayed to execute the same call again from the victim's smart account.

title: Enable Mode Signature can be replayed
reason: The enableModeSignature has no nonce, so the same signature can reinstall a module after it was uninstalled.

title: H-04. Missing nonce in `_getEnableModeDataHash()` allows signature replay
reason: A captured enable-mode signature can be replayed to reinstall a validator, which can then sign userOps and move the account's assets.

title: fallback() logic prevents hook's postCheck from getting executed
reason: The fallback skips the hook postCheck, which bypasses a validation layer, but the released text does not show a value path to an attacker.

title: Enable Mode Signature ignores module type
reason: The enable-mode signature does not cover moduleType, so a module can be installed under a more privileged type than the signer approved.

title: K1Validator.validateUserOp() validation can be bypassed
reason: tryRecoverCalldata returns address(0) on failure, matching an uninitialised owner, so a forged userOp passes validation and the account can be drained.

title: Missing nonce in _getEnableModeDataHash() allows signature replay
reason: Duplicate of H-04: missing nonce in _getEnableModeDataHash allows replay of an enable-mode signature and account takeover.

title: Peg-In Amounts May Be Stolen By Manipulating tx.gasprice
reason: Refund is gasUsed*tx.gasprice taken from the peg-in amount; a submitter/block builder controlling refundAddress can capture the peg-in.

title: Insuﬃcient PSBT validation
reason: A malicious signing-round peer/coordinator can add an unchecked output to the PSBT and redirect BTC from the bridge multisig.

title: Invalid Proof Causes Early Return For Multiple Calls To mint()
reason: An invalid proof short-circuits validation so later mint() calls in the same tx are credited without proof, minting unbacked BTC.

title: transaction.value Is Used To Refund Invalid Burns
reason: The invalid-burn refund uses transaction.value rather than the burned amount, so an attacker is refunded more than burned and can mint unbounded tokens.

title: No Duplication Checks For Peg-In Proofs
reason: A valid peg-in proof can be duplicated inside one mint() call, multiplying the minted BTC.

title: Peg-In Proofs Are Only Veriﬁed For Top-level Calls
reason: Proof checks only run when the mint() call is the top-level call, so a contract calling mint() bypasses proof verification and mints BTC.

title: The rewards can be abused within 1 block
reason: supply/requestWithdrawal/repay/redeemBond in one block captures all rewards accrued for the round.

title: Front-running for the bid() method
reason: bid() can be front-run, but the released body is withheld (publisher notice) and the gain is a better bid allocation, not a demonstrated value transfer.

title: The rewards can be doubled
reason: _handleRoundRepay never stores roundLastDistribution, so calling repay twice pays the same round reward twice.

title: Lenders may receive more rewards then than they should
reason: A lender's rewards keep accruing past the round's repayment, so they receive more than their share.

title: The rewards can be abused within 1 block via NFT transfer
reason: Rewards can be claimed again after transferring the bondNFT to a second account.

title: Incorrect scaling in _calculateWantAmount
reason: _calculateWantAmount mixes 18-decimal and asset decimals, so the wanted amount is mis-scaled, but the text does not establish that the caller profits rather than reverting or under-filling.

title: Lack of State Rollback in Callback Function
reason: The callback does not roll back state when the storage-deposit promise fails, an accounting error, but no attacker value path is shown.

title: Potential user losses due to manipulated amount_out
reason: A crafted swap path accumulates amount_out repeatedly, letting the attacker move the vault's price limit and profit at the user's expense.

title: Incorrect token account and corresponding authority used in function close_bot()
reason: close_bot uses the quote-token account/authority when revenue_token is the base token, so the caller withdraws from the protocol account.

title: Lack of lock during the withdrawals from Ref-Exchange
reason: Repeated execute_dca in one block re-enters Ref-Exchange withdraw and pulls the protocol's funds.

title: Incorrect refund balance in Function after_wrap_near_for_create_bot()
reason: Wrapped NEAR is not counted after a failed min-amount check, giving an incorrect refund balance; direction of gain is not established.

title: Unscaled expo values in Pyth-Oracle integration
reason: Pyth expo is not applied, so the oracle price can be wrong, but the text does not fix which side gains.

title: Partial Liquidations won't be possible for vaults with the collateral asset of decimals < 18
reason: gainedShares rounds to zero for <18-decimal collateral, so partial liquidation is impossible and the borrower keeps an unliquidated position; the text shows no direct attacker transfer.

title: Reentrancy allows anyone to modify beneficiary between the bundle and steal assets
reason: The executor can re-enter through the flasher callback or an ETH withdrawal and reset the beneficiary, so the settled bundle pays the attacker.

title: Anyone can override the handler records using the same trasnferId and failing bundle
reason: Anyone can call xReceive again with the same transferId and a failing bundle to overwrite the handler record that holds dormant funds.

title: Using the user’s router allowance, anyone can steal user’s funds
reason: With sender=receiver=victim and an attacker-chosen vault, _safePullTokenFrom spends the victim's router allowance into the attacker's vault.

title: Using SWAP as an action, anyone can steal user's funds from router
reason: The SWAP action lacks the beneficiary check, so a victim's permit/allowance can be used to swap the withdrawn funds to the attacker.

title: Frontrunning Permit allows the user to do a different set of actions than the beneficiary intended and, in the worst case run away with funds
reason: A user permit can be front-run and reused for a different action set, letting the attacker route the funds away.

title: multiTransferFrom() Could Lead to Draining All Native Tokens
reason: multiTransferFrom can be driven to move all native-token balance held by Hinkal to the caller (lead only: no released report body).

title: Arithmetic Overflow in Circom Could Be Exploited to Drain Funds
reason: Field-arithmetic overflow in the Circom swap circuit lets a large-value commitment pass the comparison and be withdrawn (lead only).

title: The Protocol Can Be Drained Through Commitment Duplication
reason: An empty inputNullifiers array keeps the transfer circuit valid, so commitments are inserted without nullifying the old ones and the same deposit is withdrawn repeatedly (lead only).

title: Unconstrained calldataHash Could Lead to Attackers Re-Routing Funds
reason: calldataHash is not constrained, so a valid proof can be replayed with different external-call data and the withdrawn funds re-routed (lead only).

title: Potential Malleability Attacks on Nullifier Due to Groth16
reason: Groth16 malleability would give a second proof for the same nullifier, but the text does not demonstrate the double spend.

title: Insufficient Validation of Access Token Existence
reason: An internal Merkle node can be proven to pass the access-token check, but the released text gives no value path after the bypass.

title: An attacker can force 0 shares to be minted for a liquidity provider
reason: A max short front-run pushes shareReserves to zero so the victim addLiquidity mints 0 shares and their capital accrues to the attacker's existing shares.

title: First LP can steal subsequent LP provisions
reason: The first LP donates to inflate assets and front-runs the next depositor so their yield shares mint as zero, then redeems the whole pool.

title: Reentrancy in StEthHyperdrive.openShort
reason: The ETH refund callback in StEthHyperdrive._deposit re-enters openShort before reserves are updated, getting a better price on the second half and draining the pool.

title: Governance fees are part of share reserves when closing non-matured longs
reason: Governance fees remain inside share reserves when closing non-matured longs, so a trader can trade them out and governance cannot claim them.

title: Governance fees are part of share reserves when opening shorts
reason: Governance fees remain inside share reserves when opening shorts, so a trader can extract them.

title: Drain pool by sandwiching matured shorts
reason: Front-running the checkpoint of a matured short after opening a max short moves the curve and lets the attacker close at a profit absorbed by LPs (coded PoC: 72,584 -> 741,169 base).

title: Exchange rate calculation is vulnerable to first-depositor attack
reason: First-depositor donation inflates the exchange rate and dilutes the next depositor (mitigated only partially by dead shares).

title: Auto-Compounding Can Lead To Liquidations
reason: Auto-compounding can push a position into liquidation, but the gain is an ordinary liquidation bounty, not a demonstrated attacker profit.

title: Collateral-Free Borrows
reason: In the borrow callback, before the tokenId borrow balance is written, the attacker redeems the NFTLP collateral and keeps both the NFT and the borrowed funds.

title: Manipulation of oracle price by pushing malicious pool
reason: A malicious pool pushed into the oracle's pool list feeds a manipulated TWAP/harmonic liquidity and lets the attacker borrow or liquidate at the wrong price.

title: Legitimate deployment can use newly created UniswapV3Pool with manipulated TWAP price
reason: A freshly created UniswapV3Pool with a manipulated 30-minute TWAP is used to deploy a TokenizedUniswapV3Position and borrow against inflated collateral.

title: Cross-contract reentrancy attack during borrow attack allows for draining the contract
reason: Cross-contract reentrancy during borrow drains the pool's liquidity.

title: Incorrect extract of inFrom_ address
reason: inFrom_ is mis-extracted from callbackData_, bypassing the DEX allowlist or fee accounting, but no direct attacker gain is shown.

title: Possible reward overpayment
reason: The reward-rate time window can overpay rewards beyond what accrued, and the excess is claimable.

title: Possible bad debt in StETHQueue
reason: When repay exceeds stETHAmount the borrower has no incentive to repay, keeping borrowed ETH as bad debt against the Liquidity contract.

title: BigMathVault library contains math error that causes debtFactor to be calculated completely wrong
reason: The wrong debtFactor underestimates the liquidated position, but the text does not show who captures the difference.

title: Incorrect supplyExchangePrice calculation
reason: supplyExchangePrice mixes normal-token and raw-token units, but the released text does not establish a profitable direction for a depositor.

title: Incorrect work of UniV3CheckFallbackCLRSOracle in the first mode
reason: In the first mode the function never returns the computed rate and always reverts on the delta check, a denial of service rather than a value path.

title: Double spending
reason: A maker borrows against CollateralToken, transfers the tokens away, and withdraws again from the pool, double-spending the collateral.

title: Duplicate interactions
reason: validateInteractions does not reject duplicates, so the same signed interaction is applied twice and the user is debited twice.

title: Solver can bypass maker signature veriﬁcation
reason: validateOrder defaults isMaker=true, so a solver can pass any signature and settle poisoned orders.

title: Lack of trader signature validation allows unauthorized fund transfers
reason: The trader's signature is never validated in settle(), so a malicious maker can move the trader's approved funds.

title: Inﬂation attack
reason: The share/asset exchange rate can be inflated by repeated supply/withdraw cycles so the next depositor mints almost no shares and the attacker withdraws their deposit.

title: Arbitrary call in LendingPool.reBalance() leads to asset theft
reason: reBalance forwards arbitrary calldata to UniswapIntegration, stranding tokens that anyone can then swap out to themselves.

title: Reentrancy risk when add/remove liquidity
reason: The removeLiquidity callback lets the attacker re-enter addLiquidity at a stale share price and mint LP cheaply, then withdraw the profit.

title: Risk of lacking access control for backtracking operations
reason: enterBacktracking is permissionless, so an attacker can force historical-price mode, trade against a zero/stale price and keep the difference, or block liquidations of their own position.

title: Incorrect way to get the token price when using the chainlink oracle
reason: The arbitrum-seq-offline Chainlink flag is used on Linea/Scroll, so the availability check is wrong, but no value path is shown.

title: Incorrect getPriceNoOlderThan age
reason: getPriceNoOlderThan with age 0 makes the Pyth read revert on L2, a denial of service rather than an attacker gain.

title: Forgeable network fee
reason: networkFeeAmount is not checked against msg.value, so the attacker forges a large fee while paying little.

title: Incorrect processing of price decimal returned by chainlink
reason: Chainlink decimals are assumed to be 8, so an 18-decimal feed returns a price 1e10 too large, inflating collateral and allowing over-borrow.

title: Attacker can steal all fees from SFPM in pools with ERC777 tokens
reason: The ERC777 tokensToSend hook re-enters before s_accountFeesBase is updated, letting the attacker register liquidity with feesBase=0 and claim the pool's fees.

title: Overflow in CollateralTracker allows minting shares for free
reason: A huge shares value overflows shares*DECIMALS in the unchecked previewMint, so shares are minted for almost no assets and the vault is drained.

title: Attacker can steal all fees from SFPM in pools with ERC777 tokens
reason: Same ERC777 reentrancy in SFPM fee accounting.

title: Overflow in `CollateralTracker` allows minting shares for free
reason: Same overflow in previewMint: mint huge shares cheaply, then withdraw the collateral.

reason: SettleLongPremium adds the premium instead of deducting it, crediting the long at the pool's expense.

reason: Same sign error in SettleLongPremium: premium is added rather than deducted.

title: `UniV3TokenizedLp` can be attacked by an initial donation

reason: The helper's getPrice()/getLpPrice() can be manipulated, but the PeckShield body is withheld so no attacker value path is established.

title: Potential Drain of Funds through BaseBounty

title: Initial Liquidity Can Be Lost by Front-Running Pool Initialization

title: Eligibility Manipulation Leads to Stolen Rewards
